summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +14.2%; weakest: Oats -17.9%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.94% (-35 bp in a month), 2-year 4.56% (-32 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (-3 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.97% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.96 (+0.5% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.440 (+4.6% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.653 (-0.7%); USD/MXN 18.77 (+4.0%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.9% in a month (+10.7% YTD); VIX 19.4. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 102.95 $/bbl (+16.4% in a month), Brent 112.33, ULSD 4.655 $/gal (+3.3%), natural gas 2.88 (-14.5%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -1.7% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.3%, Hang Seng -5.4%, yuan +0.7% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 11 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (33%); S&P GSCI +3.3% in a month; gold -7.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
